description: The AIResQ team publishes high-resolution thermal drone imagery for detecting people during search-and-rescue work. The current Zenodo record describes 9,788 images up to 2048 by 1536 pixels and 17,550 person labels across an annual cycle, varied terrain, weather and time of day. Its own metadata now mark the archive open under CC BY 4.0, with public access free. The article instead described an older restricted record as available upon request; that older status does not describe the current version. The imagery can evaluate detection models before planning aerial emergency-search coverage, an inferred service-simulation use, not a tested operation. A caveat is that bounding boxes do not encode rescue time, drone endurance or terrain access. The provider's description also limits intended use to civilian research, which needs reconciliation with the CC BY label. Current and older own metadata were checked without downloading the large archive. The separate small benchmark is assessed independently; no related catalogue record was identified.
